editorial:
Imagine taking a job at a creepy, old pizza place just to pay your bills, only to find out the robot mascots come to life at night. You follow Mike, a guy who is just trying to keep his little sister safe while dealing with some heavy family trauma. The vibe is very eerie, and the setting feels like a time capsule from the 80s. It is less about jumping out of the shadows and more about the weird, creepy feeling of being watched by giant animatronic animals in a dark building.

What really works here is how the robots look; they are incredibly detailed and feel real. While the story moves a bit slow in the middle, the twists keep you interested. If you are a fan of the games, you will love the Easter eggs. For the best experience, you should definitely stream it in 4K Ultra HD on Prime Video to see all the details on the robots, or maybe add the 4K Blu-ray to your physical collection if you like owning your movies. It is a great pick for a movie night with friends who enjoy a spooky but not too scary ride.
endingExplained: In the end, the villain tries to use Mike and his sister to bring back the missing children. Mike fights back and uses the robots to destroy the bad guy. He manages to save his sister, and the animatronics finally find some peace. The movie wraps up with Mike moving on with his life, but it leaves the door open for more stories in this world.
targetAudience: Ideal for anyone who loves video game adaptations and creepy robots.
